ADDITIONAL MACT, MADHUGIRI, PARTLY ALLOWING CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR
ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 26th August, 2009 passed in MVC No.1663/2007 on the file of the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) & JMFC and Addl. MACT, Madhugiri (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal'
for brevity), seeking enhancement of compensation.
NC: 2024:KHC:45678 2.
During the pendency of the appeal, the original claimant died and his legal representatives were brought on record by the order dated 16.10.2024.

3. Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - insurance company and perused the material on record.
4.
The occurrence of the accident, injuries sustained by the original claimant and coverage of insurance are not in dispute.

For having sustained injuries due to the accident, the Tribunal has granted compensation under various heads as follows:
Channabasappa vs Shivaraju on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144977604/

sentences.text:
i) Towards pain and agony Rs.25,000/-
 ii) Towards medical and other  expenses Rs. 10,000/-
 ....................

The Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.35,000/-
alongwith interest at 6% per annum and fastened liability on respondent No.1/ owner of the Mini Tempo bearing registration No.KA-06-1370 on the reason that there was no insurance NC:
2024:KHC:45678 policy executed by the 2nd respondent in favour of respondent No.1.
6.

In the present case, from the medical evidence on record, it is proved that the original claimant has lost four teeth in upper jaw and one tooth in the lower jaw and clear socket seen in relation to two upper and right central incisors and due to the injuries, the original claimant sustained disfiguration of face.

Therefore, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- towards 'pain and suffering'
and Rs.10,000/- for medical and other expenses.
7. There is no evidence that the original claimant has suffered disability.
It is stated that the original claimant died and his legal representatives are prosecuting the appeal.
Therefore if the deceased was alive, what amount of compensation he would have been entitled to, that has to be awarded.
Accordingly, this Court is of the opinion to award global compensation of Rs.15,000/-, in addition to the compensation awarded by the Tribunal alongwith interest at 6% per annum.
Further, respondent no.1/owner of the mini Tempo was placed exparte.
It is the contention taken by the respondent No.2/insurance company that it has not issued policy to respondent No.1 in respect of the offending vehicle.
When this being the defence raised, then it is the burden on the respondent no.1/owner of the Mini Tempo to prove that there was valid insurance coverage in respect of the offending vehicle.
But, the respondent no.1/owner failed to discharge his burden and remained exparte and has not adduced evidence.
Therefore, liability fastened on respondent no.1/owner by the Tribunal is correct.
Accordingly, the findings given by the Tribunal on the liability are confirmed.
9. In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.

Channabasappa vs Shivaraju on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/144977604/
3 ii)

The impugned judgment and award dated 26th August 2009 passed in MVC No.1663/2007, on the file of the Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) & JMFC and Addl. MACT,
Madhugiri, stands modified to an extent that the appellants (legal representatives of original claimant) are entitled for an additional NC: 2024:KHC:45678 global compensation of Rs.15,000/- (Rupees fifteen thousand only), along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

However, the appellants are not entitled to interest for the period from 31.10.2012 to 16.10.2024 vide order of this Court dated 16.10.2024.
iii) The respondent no.1/owner shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
iv) All other findings and observations made by the Tribunal are kept intact.
 v) Draw the award accordingly.

SD/-
 (HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR)
